fields.v: School of Computer Science, University of Windsor, Canada (Shanto, Asaduzzaman, Ngom); Independent Researcher (Islam)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — evidence-based 16-category template for agent instruction files (10 Required, 4 Gap, 2 Recommended) with a maintenance protocol, derived from a repository-mining study of 3,387 instruction files in 1,000 AIDev GitHub repositories (adoption, cross-format consistency, maintenance); AGIT-Instruct benchmark for instruction-file generation; exploratory generation experiment (with vs without template; four template-guided configurations)

fields.v: No SDD approach. Instruction-file formats AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GitHub Copilot instructions, Cursor rules (.cursorrules); proposed evidence-based template (16 categories: 10 Required, 4 Gap, 2 Recommended) + maintenance protocol; generation configurations GPT-4o-mini zero-shot / RAG, CodeLlama-13B Base / QLoRA

Template for one instruction file: Required: Do/Don't rules, Build/run/install, Repository structure, Tooling/agent config, Examples, Domain models, Test/CI commands, API/interface contracts, Architecture, Code style; Gap: Security/secrets, Maintenance/when to update, Ownership/contacts, Git/PR conventions; Recommended: Project overview, Performance requirements (Table 4)

No development flow. Maintenance protocol with three review triggers: agent-related errors, repository changes (build, tests, structure, dependencies, interfaces), periodic accuracy checks; recorded under Maintenance/when to update
Maintainers review instruction categories after agent errors/code review and after repository changes; check consistency across formats; generated files to be treated as drafts requiring verification
Single artefact (instruction file): mined, not executed by agents; generation of instruction files by LLMs evaluated against developer-written references; no coding task run
Not classifiable (instruction / context files, no specification)
N/A for coding (no coding task); corpus of existing open-source repositories; generation task: write an instruction file from a short repository summary

1,000 repositories (500 top + 500 bottom by stars) from AIDev (932,791 PRs, 116,211 repos); 3,387 files (1,677 AGENTS.md, 1,107 CLAUDE.md, 538 Copilot, 65 cursorrules); 386 section pairs; maintenance: 5,396 heading edit events, 448 files, 283 repos, 943 PRs; AGIT-Instruct 1,815 files / 522 repos (1,432 train, 321 val, 62 eval; 556 reference category instances)
Open-source GitHub repositories, mixed languages (C# noted separately)
N/A (no participants)
Not measured

Not measured for coding agents. Generation: structural category coverage; content alignment ROUGE-1 F1 and cosine similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) on generic intents; manual intent preservation (Match / Partial / Wrong / Missing)
Not measured

Adoption rates (overall, per format, multi-format, co-occurrence, by language; logistic regression odds ratios); category- and heading-level Jaccard; instruction-level consistency (equivalent / complementary / divergent / contradictory); maintenance: touch count, ownership concentration, churn ratio, lifecycle pattern, update trigger; category addition ratio (CAR)

Automatic file detection by filename on cloned repos; manual category coding (two authors on 400 files, kappa 0.80, then one author); manual labelling of 386 section pairs by two annotators (kappa 0.85); maintenance metrics computed from AIDev PR patches; generic intents produced by GPT-4o-mini; automatic ROUGE/cosine; manual assessment of 278 RAG instances. Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Cliff's delta

Instruction-file generation on AGIT-Instruct eval set (62 files), no coding agent; criterion: coverage of template categories and alignment with developer-written references. - GPT-4o-mini without template (exploratory): coverage 0.187 (Required 0.168, Gap 0.080, Recommended 0.500). Quality: does not work (structure); cost not reported. - GPT-4o-mini zero-shot with template: coverage 0.828; full-file ROUGE-1 0.423, cos 0.681; overlap-only 0.386 / 0.710. Quality: partly. - GPT-4o-mini RAG with template: coverage 0.786; ROUGE-1 0.459, cos 0.683; overlap 0.433 / 0.708; manual 278 instances: 19.4% match, 61.2% partial, 19.4% missing, 0 wrong. Quality: partly. - CodeLlama-13B Base with template: coverage 0.645; ROUGE-1 0.304, cos 0.373; overlap 0.309 / 0.434. Quality: partly. - CodeLlama-13B QLoRA with template: coverage 0.166 (Gap 0.044); ROUGE-1 0.273, cos 0.608; overlap 0.347 / 0.647. Quality: does not work (structure). Cost verdict for all: not reported

fields.v: Template vs no template: GPT-4o-mini, same base prompt and repository inputs, only template guidance varied, on the same 62-file eval set (exploratory). Four template-guided configurations on the same repository-disjoint eval set; inputs: target format, language, popularity, short repository summary; greedy decoding for CodeLlama; RAG with 3 retrieved training examples. Repetitions: 1 (not stated otherwise). No coding agent, no acceptance tests (references are developer-written files)

Template raises coverage from 18.7% to 82.8% (3.00 to 13.25 categories per file), Gap tier 8.0% to 97.7%. Zero-shot highest coverage (0.828) > RAG 0.786 > CL Base 0.645 > CL QLoRA 0.166; RAG highest full-file ROUGE-1 (0.459 vs 0.423); QLoRA raises cosine 0.373 -> 0.608 but lowers coverage. No significance tests for generation results. Mining: adoption 66.2% top vs 50.2% bottom (OR 1.171 per log stars); multi-format 42.2% vs 21.6%; 16.1% of 386 pairs divergent, none contradictory; 40.4% single-touch files; churn differs by format (H = 31.02, p < 0.001)

Partly: benchmark separates structural coverage from content alignment and shows they diverge (QLoRA); authors call template comparison exploratory; LLM output variation not controlled; generic-intent transformation may remove operational details; downstream coding-agent effect not measured

Category coding subjective; divergence may reflect scope; generic intents abstract away commands; LLM variability; repository characteristics confound format differences; public GitHub only, four formats; category-based eval selection not representative; pairs not independent; maintenance history cannot reveal intent; impact of instruction files on coding-agent performance not measured (future work); tiers are heuristic, not proof of importance

Tables 2, 3 and Fig. 2-4 partly jumbled by pdftotext; Table 3 rows rebuilt from text (e.g. Build/run/install 959 additions, 239 deletions, CAR 0.801; Ownership 7/0, 1.000). Some lifecycle/trigger values in Fig. 4 only (text gives 52.5% proactive AGENTS.md, 65.2% co-change CLAUDE.md, 48.2% reactive Copilot). AGIT-Instruct: initial filtering gives 2,853 files from 552 repos (p. 21), the final benchmark 1,815 files from 522 repos after generic-intent filtering and repository-disjoint partitioning (p. 22); the drop of 1,038 files is not explained. Replication package: github.com/mehedisresearch/AGIT-Template (prompts and fine-tuning settings). No pre-registration. Languages: mixed

rev.why: Round 0 called 2,853 vs 1,815 files an inconsistency; the text gives 2,853 as the initial filter and 1,815 as the result after further filtering and partitioning, so it is an unexplained reduction, not a contradiction
